# dtcloud_images (Data Source)

Lists every image visible to the caller.

Every filter is applied by the provider. The endpoint's own visibility parameter only separates
public images from the rest: asking it for `private` returns private, shared and community images
together. Filtering here means `visibility = "private"` returns private images, which is what it
says.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "dtcloud_images" "private_active" {
  visibility = "private"
  status     = "active"
}

data "dtcloud_images" "ubuntu" {
  os_distro = "ubuntu"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `name` (String) Only return images with this exact name. Applied by the provider.
- `os_distro` (String) Only return images carrying this distribution. Applied by the provider.
- `status` (String) Only return images in this status, e.g. `active`. Applied by the provider.
- `visibility` (String) Only return images with this visibility. Applied by the provider, because the endpoint's own filter only separates public images from the rest.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `images` (List of Object) The images that matched, in the order the platform returned them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--images))

<a id="nestedatt--images"></a>
### Nested Schema for `images`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String)
- `min_disk` (Number)
- `name` (String)
- `os_distro` (String)
- `os_type` (String)
- `size` (String)
- `status` (String)
- `type` (String)
- `uefi` (Boolean)
- `visibility` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **How the filters match.** `name` must match exactly; `os_distro`, `visibility` and `status` ignore
  case. The whole list is fetched either way.
* **`os_type` is filled in here, and not elsewhere.** The list endpoint guesses it from `os_distro`
  when the platform holds no value. `dtcloud_image` and the resource read the details endpoint, which
  makes no such guess, so the same image can report an empty `os_type` there.
